summary: ZnS thin films were grown on GaAs and HgCdTe substrates using atomic layer deposition (ALD) at very low temperatures. The films were polycrystalline, and the growth rate and surface roughness decreased with increasing temperature. The study aimed to develop a low-temperature ALD method to prevent damage to HgCdTe substrates during film growth.
evidence: ZnS films were grown under several temperatures lower than 140 ℃. The growth temperatures range from 55 ℃ to 132 ℃ for GaAs substrate and 55 ℃ for HgCdTe. The results showed the ZnS films were polycrystalline. The growth rate monotonically decreased with temperature, as well as the root mean square (r.m.s) roughness measured by AFM. The study aimed to develop a low-temperature growth method for ALD.
